limitations: Short local Jepsen campaigns, not an exhaustive safety proof or soak.
The original crash cases used orderly termination; explicit abrupt-restart cases use the corrected forced-kill harness.
Snapshot fault campaigns do not observe the exact interruption point inside an in-flight snapshot RPC.
The printed seed is metadata; the harness does not seed all random choices and cannot replay the generated workload or execution schedule.
Host-backed filesystem/process tests do not qualify physical power loss.

limitations: Development QEMU AArch64 fixtures, four vCPUs, new host-backed virtual NVMe disks.

Abrupt termination observes acknowledged term recovery and the ordinary durable-term advancement fixture; it does not independently check same-term vote retention across a VM crash, interrupted log/snapshot publication, or physical power loss.
Two guests exercise the native Raft-backed catalog, remote invocation and generation-fenced unregister; they do not join a Java/C++/Rust TCP cluster.
No simultaneous multi-voter restart, storage fault injection, new TLA+ execution, throughput or management TLS availability qualification.

abrupt_recovery.limitation: QEMU process loss with a host-backed virtual NVMe disk; not physical power-loss qualification

native_charlotte.interrupt_guard: The kernel fixture emits the matched first-term line only after stage >= 6, leader state, term > 0, and durable == 1.

three_leader_smoke.operations_per_leader: one write and two fenced reads

docker_event_capture_note: Docker retains a bounded event history. The final event arrays omit some earlier startup/fault events; earlier complete counts observed during the campaign are retained separately. Partition and heal operations also verified actual attachment in the harness.
